title: A Clinical Study to Evaluate the Effects of Driscoll's Raspberries and Driscoll's Blackberries on Postprandial Glycemic Response, Satiety, and Consumer Appeal in Healthy Adults
official: A Clinical Study to Evaluate the Effects of Driscoll's Raspberries and Driscoll's Blackberries on Postprandial Glycemic Response, Satiety, and Consumer Appeal in Healthy Adults
summary:
This is a decentralized, single-arm, within-subject crossover clinical study evaluating the effects of Driscoll's Raspberries and Driscoll's Blackberries on postprandial glycemic response, satiety, and consumer appeal in healthy adults aged 18-65 years. Forty participants will each consume three standardized breakfast meals - a raspberry-inclusive meal, a blackberry-inclusive meal, and a sugar-reference meal - in any order over a two-week period, wearing a continuous glucose monitor (CGM) throughout.

All study activities are conducted remotely at participants' homes. CGM data will be used to compute incremental area under the glucose-time curve (iAUC) over the two-hour postprandial window following each meal. Self-reported questionnaires will assess satiety, energy, digestive comfort, and sensory appeal following each meal condition.
criteria:
Inclusion Criteria:

* Be male or female.
* Adult aged 18-65 years.
* Anyone who is generally healthy - does not live with any uncontrolled chronic disease.
* Willing and able to wear a CGM device continuously for the two-week study period.
* Willing to consume three standardized breakfast meals over the two-week study period, each consumed after an overnight fast of at least eight hours, with a minimum of 24 hours between each standardized meal event.
* Willing to purchase and eat fresh Driscoll's Raspberries and Driscoll's Blackberries from a local retailer using a sponsor-provided berry stipend for use in the standardized meals.
* Have reasonable access to a retailer that sells Driscoll's-branded raspberries and blackberries.
* Have access to a smartphone or computer with a reliable internet connection.
* Willing to maintain the same diet and exercise regimen consistently throughout the study duration.
* Willing and able to complete all required digital surveys via the Citruslabs study platform at Baseline, and at the end of the day following Meal 1, Meal 2, and Meal 3.
* Resides in the United States.

Exclusion Criteria:

* Anyone with pre-existing chronic conditions that would prevent participants from adhering to the protocol, including oncological and psychiatric disorders.
* Anyone currently undergoing treatment for cancer, or have had a serious illness requiring hospitalization in the last 3 months.
* Known or suspected allergy or hypersensitivity to raspberries, blackberries, or other berry species.
* Known or suspected allergy, intolerance, or sensitivity to oats or gluten that would prevent consumption of the standardized oat-based meal component.
* Current diagnosis of type 1 diabetes, type 2 diabetes, or prediabetes.
* Current use of any medications or supplements known to significantly affect blood glucose levels, including but not limited to: insulin, metformin, GLP-1 receptor agonists, SGLT-2 inhibitors, sulfonylureas, or other glucose-lowering agents.
* Known skin sensitivity to adhesives or prior documented adverse reaction to CGM sensors or similar transcutaneous monitoring devices.
* Presence of implanted electronic devices (e.g., pacemaker, implantable cardioverter-defibrillator) that may be contraindicated with CGM device use, per the CGM manufacturer's specifications.
* Pregnant, breastfeeding, or planning to become pregnant during the study period.
* Anyone with a history of substance abuse.
* Anyone who is currently a smoker or has been a smoker in the past three months.
* Currently partaking in another research study or will be partaking in any other research study at any point during this study's duration.
* History of an eating disorder currently requiring active clinical treatment.
